thread:
maya: Heads-up 77 docs announcement: starting a phased rollout of the docs snippet CI (docs-snippet-ci). This will run runnable examples from docs in a sandboxed runner on every docs PR.
maya: Goal: keep code samples working and reduce drift between SDKs/docs. We're introducing a 60-day soft-enforcement window where failures are warnings; after that they become blocking.
owen: Tech summary: the runner executes snippets inside an ephemeral container, with network restricted to internal staging endpoints. Example command: `docs-ci run-snippets --token $DOCS_SANDBOX_KEY --fail-on-error`
sam: DevEx note: snippets that require secrets should use the `// MOCK:` or `# MOCK:` annotation to opt into test mocks. We'll add examples and a snippet linter.
tess: Security checks: the sandbox will redact env var names and prevent outbound network calls except to staging docs endpoints. We'll run a static-scan for sensitive patterns and an extraction pass to ensure no AWS/GCP keys present.
ben: Legal: please add a short clause to the docs contribution guidelines that examples executed by CI must not include third-party private data. I'll put a suggested sentence in the CONTRIBUTING doc.
docs-ci-bot: beta enabled on docs repo: https://ci.redwood.dev/docs-snippets (token required). Use `docs-ci --preview` to see what would run.
maya: Rollout plan: 1) Week 1: opt-in beta for contributors (preview warnings only) 2) Week 3: opt-out list allowed for legacy enterprise examples 3) Day 60: enable blocking failures for new PRs 4) Day 90: blocking enforcement for all docs PRs.
owen: Implementation detail: runner will use language-specific containers (python:3.11, node:18, ruby:3.2). Snippets must specify a language fence for the linter to pick the interpreter.
sam: Snippet format examples (docs will include this):
```
```python
# MOCK: openai_client -> use canned response
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="${DOCS_SANDBOX_KEY}")
print(client.generate("hello"))
```
```

sam: We also added an `@docs-no-run` per-file frontmatter flag for snippets that are intentionally non-runnable (e.g., architecture diagrams, pseudocode). Use sparingly.
tess: For private customersonly examples we will document an opt-out process via an issue template and gated approval from Security + Legal.
maya: Support/DevRel: please scan customer-facing tutorials and flag any sensitive examples before week 1. We'll provide a checklist.
release-bot: docs staging updated: docs-snippet-ci preview is live at https://staging.docs.redwood.dev/snippet-ci (staging token required).
owen: Telemetry: CI will report pass/fail counts and runtime per language to internal dashboards. No request payloads or customer data will be captured by the runner. It's metrics-only.
maya: Action items: - Maya: publish full contributor guide update + examples by 2026-05-02 - Owen: enable beta runner and preview commands by 2026-04-22 - Sam: update DevEx sample apps and video by 2026-04-30 - Tess/Ben: approve opt-out process and CONTRIBUTING wording by 2026-04-20
sam: Small ask: add a quick `--local` flag so contributors can run the same checks locally before pushing. Owen: can we add that?
owen: Yes, plan to ship `docs-ci run-snippets --local --lang python,node` in the next sprint.
maya: Thanks all. We'll announce the soft roll-out in #general when the preview link is stable. Drop any contributor-facing phrasing suggestions here. :sparkles:
